title: AI-powered human action recognition of functional activities in stroke: a systematic review
title_zh: 基于人工智能的卒中功能活动人体动作识别：系统综述
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI)-based human activity recognition (HAR) is a promising approach for detecting functional activity in individuals with stroke, potentially enabling objective and ecologically valid assessment, monitoring and treatment. We aimed to synthesize current evidence on AI-based HAR for functional activity recognition after stroke, focusing on sensing technologies, target activities, settings, and model architectures. PubMed, Embase, WOS, and Scopus were searched and seventeen studies involving 224 individuals with stroke met the inclusion criteria. Inertial measurement units were the predominant sensing modality (12/17, 70.6%), with several studies demonstrating the feasibility of recognizing relevant functional activities using a single device. Single-sensor approaches were also used in home-based and simulated-home settings, suggesting potential for scalable and unobtrusive monitoring outside clinical environments; however, most studies were conducted in controlled clinical settings (11/17, 64.7%), with limited real-world validation to date. Convolutional neural networks were the most frequently used deep learning architecture, while Random Forest was the most common traditional machine learning method. Multimodal sensing may enrich activity characterization, although greater sensing complexity may reduce feasibility for prolonged home monitoring. Methodological and reporting limitations, including concerns regarding confounding and reproducibility, should be considered when interpreting the current evidence. Overall, single-sensor AI-based HAR appears promising for low-burden, continuous, and ecologically valid monitoring. Future research should prioritize longitudinal validation in everyday environments, transparent reporting of code and data availability, and inclusion of acute and severely impaired stroke populations to facilitate clinical translation toward objective monitoring, personalized rehabilitation, and remote care.
abstract_zh: 摘要 基于人工智能（AI）的人体活动识别（HAR）是检测卒中患者功能活动的一种有前景方法，有可能实现客观且生态学上有效的评估、监测和治疗。我们旨在综合卒中后基于人工智能的人体活动识别的现有证据，重点关注感知技术、目标活动、环境和模型架构。在PubMed、Embase、WOS和Scopus中检索，共有17项研究（涉及224名卒中患者）符合纳入标准。惯性测量单元是主要的感知模态（12/17，70.6%），多项研究表明使用单一设备识别相关功能活动是可行的。单传感器方法也用于家庭和模拟家庭环境，表明在临床环境之外实现可扩展和不干扰的监测具有潜力；然而，大多数研究是在受控临床环境中进行的（11/17，64.7%），迄今为止现实世界验证有限。卷积神经网络是最常用的深度学习架构，而随机森林是最常用的传统机器学习方法。多模态感知可能丰富活动表征，尽管更高的感知复杂性可能降低长期家庭监测的可行性。在解释现有证据时，应考虑到方法学和报告的局限性，包括混杂和可重复性方面的问题。总体而言，基于人工智能的单传感器人体活动识别似乎对低负担、连续且生态学上有效的监测具有前景。未来研究应优先开展日常环境中的纵向验证、透明报告代码和数据可用性，并纳入急性期和重度障碍卒中人群，以促进向客观监测、个性化康复和远程护理的临床转化。
